composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Green (100.0) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Green (88.6) | Client Sentiment (20%): Yellow (27.3)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Green (92.0) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Green (100.0) | Client Sentiment (20%): Yellow (72.7)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Red (45.6) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Green (81.8) | Client Sentiment (20%): Red (0.0)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Yellow (77.8) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Green (88.6) | Client Sentiment (20%): Yellow (27.3)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Red (54.3) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (58.8) | Client Sentiment (20%): Yellow (54.5)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Red (31.0) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Red (23.5) | Client Sentiment (20%): Yellow (72.7)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Refreshed 2026-10-05 -- SOURCE CHANGED per Emma (2026-10-05): total_units_sold_hubspot now = HubSpot company property total_units_all ('Total Units Sold (All)' = cumulative booked units, New Logo + Expansion; booked, not live), matched via findigs_company_id. Replaces prior SUM(units__c) across closed-won deals (that field was total portfolio size, not units sold -- 2026-09-04 note). sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs (Sigma, current month) / total units sold * 100. JSON keys unchanged for dashboard binding. Unscored, contextual.
accounts.completed_applications_source: Refreshed 2026-10-05 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), User Application Funnel (PostHog-sourced), window 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-05 (rolling trailing 90d). completed_applications_90d = SUM(HIT_SUBMIT); application_funnel_total_90d = COUNT. Unscored, contextual.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

median_ttd_hours.source: Refreshed 2026-10-05 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), window 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-05 (rolling trailing 90d), Groups BI, GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true, median(TIME_TO_DECISION_HOURS) split by GROUP_STATUS. Band cuts: Green<44h / Yellow 44-60 / Red>60 (empirical reconstruction, unchanged from 9/2 build, reproduces all baseline bands exactly).
median_ttd_hours.median_note: Blended all-status median not recomputed this refresh (approved/declined medians only); the rubric bands on worse_of_two, unchanged.

approval_rate_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-10-05 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), window 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-05 (rolling trailing 90d) -- same population as median_ttd_hours. FS accounts capped at Yellow max per Scoring Matrix V2 ('Cap FS at yellow').

qa_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-10-05 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), window 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-05 (rolling trailing 90d), Groups BI, decision status ILIKE %QA% share of decisioned. Band cuts Green<15 / Yellow 15-20 / Red>20 (empirical reconstruction, reproduces all baseline bands exactly).

override_rate_pct.note: Has Decision Override only applies for DecisionAssist accounts (Sigma field definition).
override_rate_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-10-05 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), window 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-05 (rolling trailing 90d), Groups BI, HAS_DECISION_OVERRIDE=true share of decisioned. ENT/MM Green<=3/Yellow3-6/Red>6; SMB not gated (always Green when data exists), per baseline convention.
override_rate_pct.split_note: Directional split (DA-declined-final-approved vs DA-approved-final-declined) not recomputed this refresh -- blended HAS_DECISION_OVERRIDE rate only.

support_ticket_ratio_per_100.source: Refreshed 2026-10-05 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), window 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-05 (rolling trailing 90d), Support Cases BI, CASE_IS_DELETED=false, excludes CASE_USER_TYPE ILIKE applic/guarant/NULL. Thresholds Green<=15/Yellow15-50/Red>50 (8/18 recalibration).

tes_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-10-05 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), window 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-05 (rolling trailing 90d) -- same population as support_ticket_ratio_per_100; numerator = SUPPORT_CASE_HAS_TECH_ESCALATION (technical escalations, NOT tenant experience -- corrected 2026-09-04). ENT<=3/3-6/>6; MM & SMB <2/2-5/>5 (SMB provisional).

volume_trend_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-10-05 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), window 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-05 (rolling trailing 90d), Groups BI, trailing 90d vs prior 90d, GROUP_IS_SUBMITTED=true. composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Red (64.3) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (66.7) | Client Sentiment (20%): Yellow (71.4)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used).
